name: Hall_2012 (SYNERGY)
review: Hall T, Beecham S, Bowes D, Gray D, Counsell S. A Systematic Literature Review on Fault Prediction Performance in Software Engineering. IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 38(6):1276-1304, 2012. doi:10.1109/TSE.2011.103
labels: SYNERGY v1.0 (doi:10.34894/HE6NAQ, CC0), dataset Hall_2012: 8,793 records, 104 label_included. Collected by Yu et al., doi:10.1007/s10664-017-9587-0.
fetch: python -m evals.fetch_data synergy  (needs `pip install synergy-dataset`). Writes evals/data/synergy/Hall_2012.csv; abstracts are reconstructed from OpenAlex inverted indexes and must not be republished in plaintext, so evals/data/ is gitignored.
question: Which empirical studies build and evaluate models that predict faults in units of a software system?
objective: Identify empirical studies, published January 2000 to December 2010, that predict faults in units of a software system, with faults in code as the dependent variable.

criteria.name: Empirical study
criteria.question: Is the paper an empirical study?

criteria.name: Predicts faults in software units
criteria.question: Is it focused on predicting faults in units of a software system?

criteria.name: Faults in code are the output
criteria.question: Are faults in code the main output (dependent variable)?

criteria.name: Not an excluded topic
criteria.question: Is it NOT focused on testing, fault injection, inspections, reliability modelling, aspects, effort estimation, debugging, faults relating to memory leakage, nano-computing or fault tolerance?

criteria.name: Not fault detection or localisation
criteria.question: Is it NOT about the detection or localisation of existing individual known faults?

criteria.name: Published 2000-2010
criteria.question: Was it published between January 2000 and December 2010?

criteria.name: English journal or conference paper
criteria.question: Is it reported in a paper published in English as a journal paper or in conference proceedings?

criteria_source: Hall et al. 2012, Section 2.2 and Table 2 (inclusion/exclusion criteria) and Section 2.3 (publication window), applied as written apart from being phrased as questions. The review's de-duplication rule (keep the most comprehensive of repeated studies) is not applied: it needs the other candidates, which a per-abstract screen does not see.
